Few jobs offer the same satisfaction as taking raw materials and shaping them into something lasting, useful, and beautifully made. That blend of creativity and practical problem-solving is what drew me to carpentry, and building spaces and furniture that people rely on every day gives my work a strong sense of purpose and pride. It is for this reason that I am certain of my desire to continue developing as a Carpenter. I am originally from Spain, and alongside my practical route into the trade I also completed a postgraduate degree at master level at a university among the world's 500 best. That experience strengthened the way I approach planning, detail, and seeing a project through. Across my work, I have completed 2 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing how much I value precise workmanship, accurate reading of a space, efficient planning, and clean, durable finishes that balance function with visual appeal.

When I moved into an unfamiliar area of work, I did not rush it; instead, I repeated the same methods until the process became natural, which took roughly a year. In day-to-day tasks, I handle the standard issues of the job by following the documented process, and when a case falls outside it, I bring it to a senior colleague so the work keeps moving correctly. I take part in team exchanges and, when someone needs it, I explain my own section of the work clearly so others can pick up the next stage without delay. On one long assignment that ran into repeated setbacks, I stayed with it through the frustrating stages and worked extra hours when necessary until it was finished.

One of my favourite memories was bringing my family to see a community project I had helped build, only for my youngest relative to run straight to a bench I had made and proudly call it “our family bench.” That moment captured exactly why this trade matters to me. I am now looking to bring that same care, steadiness, and sense of purpose to a carpentry role where I can contribute reliable work that people will use for years.

Few things are more rewarding than watching a child meet a new idea with uncertainty and then, moments later, with a smile of recognition. That moment is what drew me to primary education and continues to shape the kind of teacher I want to be: someone who helps children build confidence, curiosity, and a positive foundation for lifelong learning. I am especially motivated by the chance to make the classroom a place where every child feels seen, encouraged, and capable. My approach centres on turning complex topics into engaging, age-appropriate lessons that invite participation and understanding across a wide range of learning styles, so that pupils remain involved and supported in their progress. This direction is grounded in a postgraduate degree at master level completed at a university among the world's 100 best, where I also completed 3 projects with tangible outcomes. Originally from the Netherlands, I bring that background into my wider perspective while keeping my focus firmly on the needs of the children and communities I serve.

In practice, I build my teaching through steady preparation and careful follow-through. When I needed to work with a new set of methods, I spent around eight weeks practising them deliberately before using them confidently in my work. In another setting, I reworked a clumsy part of an existing procedure, and a frequent error that had kept recurring stopped appearing. Colleagues also ask me from time to time for my opinion on topics within my speciality, which I value because it reflects the collaborative side of education. Just as importantly, I finish the work handed to me as agreed and on time, whether that involves planning, delivery, or day-to-day responsibilities.

One of my favourite memories came during a school reading event, when a younger family member proudly introduced me as “the teacher who makes stories come alive.” It was funny, warm, and deeply affirming. That moment captured exactly why I love this profession, and I am eager to bring that same sense of encouragement, clarity, and care to a primary classroom.

Few fields sit so naturally at the meeting point of creativity and commercial impact as marketing, and that balance is what continues to draw me to it. I have always been fascinated by what makes people connect with a message, brand, or idea, and marketing felt like the right way to combine creative thinking with strategic decision-making to support meaningful business growth. That interest became especially real on a family trip when we unexpectedly came across a storefront promotion built around a campaign concept I had helped shape; before I said anything, my family started pointing out the display with excitement, and seeing work I had contributed to appear so visibly in the real world made the profession feel immediate and worthwhile. Originally from Ghana, I completed an undergraduate degree at bachelor level at a university outside the major international rankings, and that academic foundation gave me a practical route into understanding how ideas can be developed into work with tangible outcomes. I have completed 1 project with a tangible outcome, which reinforced my interest in turning insight into campaigns that resonate with real audiences and produce measurable results.

I have particularly enjoyed the side of marketing that involves translating audience data into clear campaign direction while keeping brand storytelling connected to performance outcomes. For example, when I needed to use a new software tool in my work, it took well over a year of regular practice before it began to feel familiar, and that experience taught me the value of building confidence through steady use rather than expecting instant fluency. In day-to-day work, I handle standard cases by following the documented process, and when something falls outside that pattern, I ask a senior colleague so the work can move forward correctly. I also take part in team exchanges and explain my own section of the work when someone needs context or an update. Just as importantly, I do what my role requires and meet the deadlines that are set. Looking ahead, I want to continue growing as a Marketing Manager by contributing clear thinking, reliable execution, and a strong interest in campaigns that connect with people and support lasting business results.

Movement matters most when it gives someone back a part of life they feared had narrowed, and that belief is what led me to physiotherapy. Inspired by the way movement can restore confidence, independence, and quality of life, I chose this profession to combine my interest in health science with a deeply practical, people-focused career. A defining part of my approach is turning clinical assessment into tailored, achievable rehabilitation plans that patients can follow with confidence, using evidence-based treatment and clear communication to support recovery both physically and emotionally. My academic route includes a postgraduate degree at master level completed at a university among the world's 100 best, and I bring to practice the perspective of someone from Germany who values precise reasoning alongside compassionate care. This interest became especially meaningful to me through seeing how small, well-chosen exercises can change how people feel about their own progress, and it continues to shape my ambition to help patients return to the activities that matter most to them.

To gain insight, I have repeatedly stepped into unfamiliar territory and learned quickly enough to contribute in real terms: in one project, I absorbed an unfamiliar discipline in less than a month and was soon working at the level expected of a long-standing specialist. For example, when a difficult problem had already resisted several more experienced colleagues, I devised a new method to address it; that approach is now used well beyond the original group. In day-to-day work, this has also meant becoming the person many colleagues turn to when a hard question arises, whatever the area, because they know I will work through the issue carefully and help move it forward. Upon reflection, the same pattern shaped a slower project that met repeated obstacles; I kept it on track by continuing through additional evenings until the work was completed, contributing to 4 completed projects with tangible outcomes.

Beyond formal settings, one of my favourite family memories captures why this career feels so personal: after I showed a relative a simple balance exercise I often teach patients, the whole family turned it into a playful living-room “rehab challenge” during a holiday gathering. Looking ahead, I want to bring that same sense of structure, encouragement, and shared progress to every physiotherapy role I take on.
